_comment: S3 lifecycle policy — agrisync-raw-ap-south-1 (the raw-blob / voice-evidence
cold-tier bucket).
spec: FINAL_SERVER_AUTHORITATIVE_EXECUTION_PLAN §11 (S11-infra-author)
Owner: infra-cofounder (author-only) + founder (apply). AUTHORED, NOT APPLIED.
🛑🛑 READ THIS BEFORE TOUCHING THIS FILE. 🛑🛑
A draft of this exact task once applied a bucket-wide NoncurrentVersionExpiration
+ ExpiredObjectDeleteMarker rule to this bucket, reasoning from a noncurrent-
version measurement taken on shramsafal-uploads-prod and wrongly generalised
to this bucket. Measured HERE, independently, 2026-08-15 (read-only,
aws s3api list-object-versions --bucket agrisync-raw-ap-south-1):
current objects:     41  (943 KB)
noncurrent versions: 178 (129 MB)
delete markers:      178, ALL of them IsLatest=true
That last line is the trap: every one of those 178 keys has NO current
version — the object was deleted and only the noncurrent (pre-delete)
version still holds the bytes. Those bytes are raw farmer voice recordings
and complete DPDP personal-data export ZIPs, per the plan's own data-
ownership matrix, and — per this plan section — exist in NO backup at all.
A NoncurrentVersionExpiration/ExpiredObjectDeleteMarker rule here would
delete 99.3% of this bucket's bytes, irrecoverably, on first lifecycle run.
D9 CHECK (founder ruling: voice audio is retained FOREVER, nothing ages
out): this bucket is exactly the one D9 governs. This file contains ONE
rule, and it is not an expiration, transition, or deletion of any kind —
see below. There is no Expiration, no Transitions, no
NoncurrentVersionExpiration, no NoncurrentVersionTransitions, and no
ExpiredObjectDeleteMarker anywhere in this document, deliberately. If a
future edit to this file adds any of those, it must be re-checked against
D9 before it is authored, not just before it is applied.
LIVE POLICY CAPTURED VERBATIM 2026-08-15 (READ-ONLY, aws s3api
get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket agrisync-raw-ap-south-1):
NoSuchLifecycleConfiguration — this bucket has NO lifecycle policy today.
Rollback for this file is 'delete the lifecycle configuration entirely':
aws s3api delete-bucket-lifecycle --bucket agrisync-raw-ap-south-1 --region ap-south-1
(also saved verbatim by apply-config.sh into the capture/ subfolder it
creates at run time, timestamped, so the rollback record is never only
in this file).
THE ONE RULE THIS FILE ADDS: AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload after 7 days.
This is the ONLY lifecycle action the plan explicitly names as safe on
this bucket ('AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload is safe on both and can
proceed'). It cannot delete or move a completed object — it only cleans
up multipart uploads that were started and never finished (a stuck upload
leaves an unbilled-looking but real cost, and blocks nothing by cleaning
up after 7 days).
The 178 noncurrent versions / delete markers above are DELIBERATELY left
untouched pending a founder retention decision on raw evidence noncurrent
versions (per this plan section: 'requiring a retention decision, not as
garbage'). Do not add a rule here until that decision is made and
explicitly re-checked against D9.
This bucket's bucket-policy is authored in TWO PARTS — see
bucket-policy.json (safe to apply now) and
bucket-policy-cmk-deny-rail.PHASE2-DO-NOT-APPLY.json (NOT safe to apply
until the backend RawBlobStore CMK binding lands — see that file's header
for the ordering hazard).
APPLY (founder only, via apply-config.sh):
bash aws/raw/apply-config.sh --apply
VERIFY:
aws s3api get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket agrisync-raw-ap-south-1 --region ap-south-1
